question.problem:
Consider the following trigonometric equation: 

$$
\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{x}{2}-\frac{\pi }{3})=-1
$$

The general solution of this equation can be expressed as 

$$
x=a\pi +2n\pi ,
$$

where $n$ is any integer. Find a possible value of $a$ in the range $[0,2).$

$a=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The given equation is equivalent to 

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{x}{2}-\frac{\pi }{3})=-1.
$$

So, the general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{2}-\frac{\pi }{3} & =-\frac{\pi }{4}+n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the above equation for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{2} & =\frac{\pi }{3}-\frac{\pi }{4}+n\pi  \\ \frac{x}{2} & =\frac{\pi }{12}+n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{\pi }{6}+2n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that $a=\frac{1}{6}.$
